intended_object: The integral representation (ℤ[M]-module) of a monoid M given by an abelian group G on which M acts by group automorphisms, written additively. This is the standard way to view, e.g., the units of a Galois extension as a Galois module. Inferred from the docstring.
explanation: The body is `Rep.of (Representation.ofMulDistribMulAction M G)`. That representation sends g : M to the ℤ-linear endomorphism a ↦ ofMul (g • toMul a) of `Additive G`. It is ℤ-linear because the action is multiplicative-distributive, so each g acts as a group endomorphism, and every additive endomorphism is ℤ-linear. This is exactly the intended object. The hypotheses are the natural ones. G must be a commutative group so that `Additive G` is an abelian group, which a ℤ-module needs. M only has to be a monoid, and `MulDistribMulAction` is precisely an action by group endomorphisms. The definition just wraps Mathlib's existing `Representation.ofMulDistribMulAction` as an object of the category `Rep ℤ M`, so it is not too narrow either.
